name: Full-text search
explanation: Searching large amounts of text by words and relevance rather than exact matches, often tolerating typos.

triggers: search;find;typos;search through
requirements: Search with a real full-text index, not LIKE with a leading wildcard;Handle typos, plurals and different word forms;Rank results by relevance and highlight the matching words;Debounce search as you type and limit the number of results;Search only data the user may see, or filter the results by permission
done_when: Common misspellings still find the right results;Users never see results they have no access to

name: User comments
explanation: Letting users post, reply to, edit and moderate comments on content such as posts or products.
synonyms: comment section;comment thread;replies
triggers: comment on;leave a comment;reply to;comments under;add comments;discussion

done_when: Posting a script tag shows it as plain text;Users can only edit or delete their own comments, while moderators can remove any

name: Maps and location
explanation: Showing places on an interactive map and finding the user's location, with services such as Google Maps, Mapbox or the browser's Geolocation API.

triggers: show on a map;near me;user's location;where they are;nearest store;distance
requirements: Ask for location only when the user does something that needs it;Handle permission denied, and offer to type a place instead;Restrict map API keys to your own domains;Provide a text list of the locations as well as the map;Do not track location in the background without a clear reason and consent
done_when: Denying location still lets the user find places;Keyboard and screen reader users get the same information without the map

name: PDF generation
explanation: Creating PDF files such as invoices, tickets or reports from app data, on the server or in the browser.

triggers: download as pdf;invoice pdf;print to pdf;create an invoice;printable

done_when: Generated PDFs look the same in every viewer;Users can only download documents they are allowed to see

name: Data export
explanation: Letting users download data as a file, such as CSV or Excel, often generated in the background for large exports.
synonyms: csv export;excel export;download data
triggers: as a spreadsheet;to excel;as csv;download their data;export to;download as
requirements: Export only data the user is allowed to see;Build large exports in the background, and notify the user when ready;Write CSV as UTF-8 with a byte order mark so Excel shows special characters;Prefix cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return with a single quote to stop formula injection;Include clear column headers and the export date

name: Data import
explanation: Letting users upload a file such as CSV or Excel to create many records at once, with validation and a report of rows that failed.
synonyms: csv import;bulk import;excel import;bulk upload
triggers: import from;upload a csv;upload a spreadsheet;import users;many at once;from excel
requirements: Validate every row, and report errors by row and column;Show a preview before importing;Import large files in the background and show progress;Make imports safe to repeat, so importing a file twice creates no duplicates;Limit file size and accept only the expected file types
done_when: A file with some bad rows reports exactly what to fix;Importing the same file again creates no duplicates

name: Analytics and event tracking
explanation: Measuring how people use the app, such as page views, clicks and sign-ups, with tools like Google Analytics, PostHog or Plausible.
synonyms: analytics;event tracking;usage tracking;telemetry;funnel
triggers: how many users;track clicks;which pages;usage statistics;track visitors;conversion rate
requirements: Ask for consent before tracking where the law requires it;Never send personal data such as emails or names to analytics;Give events clear, consistent names, and document them;Track the events that answer real product questions;Let analytics fail silently without breaking the app
done_when: Key events appear in analytics with the expected properties;No personal data shows up in analytics reports

name: Transactional email
explanation: Automatic emails sent because of something a user did, such as a welcome message, a receipt or a password reset, through a service like SendGrid or Amazon SES.
synonyms: email notifications;smtp;email service
triggers: send an email;send email;welcome email;confirmation email;email when;receipt email;email the user
requirements: Send emails from a background job with retries;Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for the sending domain;Include a plain-text version as well as HTML;Use templates, and test them in common email apps;Never put passwords in emails, and make any links or codes in them single-use and short-lived
done_when: Emails arrive in the inbox, not in spam;Emails display correctly in major email apps, including dark mode

name: SMS messages
explanation: Sending text messages to users' phones through a provider such as Twilio, for alerts, reminders or verification codes.
synonyms: sms;text message;twilio
triggers: send an sms;text the user;send a text;message their phone
requirements: Get consent, and offer a way to opt out, such as replying STOP;Store phone numbers in the international E.164 format;Rate-limit sending to prevent abuse and high costs;Keep messages short and name the sender;Handle delivery failures and invalid numbers
done_when: Users who opted out receive no more messages;A flood of requests cannot send thousands of messages

name: Online payments
explanation: Taking money from customers through a payment provider such as Stripe or PayPal, including one-off payments, subscriptions and refunds.
synonyms: payment gateway;stripe;paypal;checkout;billing
triggers: charge customers;take payments;pay online;credit card;monthly plan;subscription;accept payments;refund
requirements: Use the provider's hosted checkout or card fields, so card data never touches your server;Confirm success from a verified webhook, not only from the browser redirect;Use idempotency keys so a retry never charges twice;Store amounts as whole numbers in the smallest unit, such as cents, with a currency;Handle failed payments, refunds and disputes;Ask users to confirm again before sensitive actions, such as changing payout details;Confirm high-risk transactions with a code tied to the amount and payee the user was shown
done_when: Paying works end to end in the provider's test mode;A double click or a retry never creates two charges

name: Filters and faceted search
explanation: Letting users narrow a list of results with filters such as price range, brand or category, often shown in a sidebar with counts.
synonyms: faceted navigation;filters;filter sidebar;facets
triggers: filter by;filter products;price range;narrow down;by category;refine results
requirements: Show how many results each filter value has;Keep filter choices in the URL so results can be shared and survive a reload;Update results without losing the scroll position or focus;Offer a clear all filters button;Make filters usable with the keyboard and on small screens;Announce the updated result count to screen readers with a live region
done_when: Applying and clearing filters always gives correct results and counts;Reloading or sharing the URL keeps the same filters

name: Shopping cart
explanation: A place where shoppers collect the items they want to buy, with quantities, prices and a running total, before going to pay.
synonyms: shopping basket;cart;basket;persistent cart
triggers: add to cart;add to basket;my basket;cart total;change quantity in cart;remove from cart;cart icon with count;keep cart after login;cart on another device
requirements: Recalculate prices, discounts and totals on the server, never trust prices sent from the browser;Keep the cart after reload and merge a guest cart into the account cart on login;Check stock and current prices again before payment and tell the user what changed;Set a maximum quantity, reject negative or non-whole numbers and treat zero as removing the line;Make quantity changes and remove buttons keyboard accessible and announce the new total;Show which variant (size, colour) each line is and link back to the product
done_when: A guest cart survives a reload and is still there after signing in;Changing a price on the server updates the cart total before checkout;Editing a quantity with only the keyboard updates the total and screen readers hear it

name: Product catalog
explanation: The organised list of everything a shop sells, where each product has a title, description, images, price and identifier, grouped into collections shoppers can browse.

triggers: list my products;products page;product categories;add a new product;product photos and descriptions;browse products;shop items list;organise products into groups
requirements: Give each product a stable unique id and a readable URL handle that does not change when the title changes;Keep draft, active and archived states so unfinished products are not shown to shoppers;Store prices as whole minor units with a currency, not floating point numbers;Give every product image alt text and serve resized versions;Let one product belong to several collections, either picked by hand or by rules such as tag or type;Mark up product pages with Product structured data and keep it matching the visible price and stock
done_when: Draft and archived products never appear on the storefront or in search;Every product has a working URL, image alt text and a price with currency;Renaming a product does not break existing links

name: Product variants and options
explanation: Lets one product come in choices such as size and colour, where every combination is its own variant with its own SKU, price, stock and picture.
synonyms: product options;sku variants;variant matrix;option values;size and colour options
triggers: choose size and colour;different sizes;size selector;pick a colour for the product;each size has its own price;out of stock in this size;t-shirt in several colours
requirements: Track stock, price and SKU per variant, not per product;Mark combinations that do not exist or are out of stock instead of letting them be added to the cart;Update price, image and stock in place when the shopper picks an option, and announce the change;Label colour swatches with the colour name, not by colour alone;Keep the selected variant in the URL so it can be shared and reloaded;Generate variants from option combinations and let the merchant remove ones that are not sold
done_when: Picking an unavailable combination never allows adding it to the cart;The price and image change when an option changes and a shared link opens the same variant;Swatches have text names that screen readers read

name: Inventory tracking
explanation: Keeps count of how many of each item are in stock at each location, lowers the count when something sells and stops the shop from selling more than it has.
synonyms: stock management;stock levels;inventory management;stock control;inventory quantities
triggers: how many are left;out of stock;low stock alert;stock count;stop overselling;only 3 left;stock in two warehouses;sold out label
requirements: Change stock with an atomic update or lock so two buyers cannot get the last item;Track quantity per variant and per location;Decide per product whether to stop selling at zero or allow overselling;Record every stock change with a reason (sale, return, restock, correction) and who made it;Put stock back when an order is cancelled or a return is restocked;Send low-stock alerts at a threshold set by the merchant
done_when: Two buyers checking out the last item at the same time give one success and one sold-out message;Every stock change can be traced to an order or a person;Cancelling an order restores the stock

name: Temporary reservation holds
explanation: Holds a limited item, seat or time slot for a customer for a short time while they pay, and frees it again if they do not finish in time.
synonyms: inventory hold;soft reservation;seat hold;cart reservation;hold timer
triggers: hold the seat while paying;reserve item during checkout;your items are held for 10 minutes;release if not paid;countdown timer at checkout;stop two people buying the same seat
requirements: Create the hold atomically so the same item cannot be held twice;Store an expiry time on the hold and release expired holds with a job, not only when someone looks;Make the payment session expire at or before the hold so nobody pays for a released item;Show the time left clearly and warn before it runs out, with a way to ask for more time;Turn the hold into a sale only after the provider confirms payment, using a webhook;Free the hold right away when the customer cancels or the payment fails

name: Pre-orders and backorders
explanation: Lets customers buy an item that is not in stock yet, either charging now or later, and ships it when the stock arrives.
synonyms: preorder;backorder;deferred purchase;continue selling when out of stock;made to order
triggers: buy before it is released;order when out of stock;ships later;coming soon but can buy;pay when it ships;expected shipping date;reserve a product before launch
requirements: Say clearly on the product page and at checkout that it is a pre-order, and when it is expected to ship;Decide whether to charge in full, take a deposit or save the card and charge on shipping;Keep consent to charge later and store the payment method with the provider, not on your server;Keep pre-order lines separate so the rest of the order can ship now;Email customers if the date slips and let them cancel for a refund;Cap pre-order quantity if supply is limited
done_when: Customers see the expected date before paying and on their receipt;A delayed date sends an update with an option to cancel;Charging later works with a saved payment method in test mode

name: Product bundles
explanation: Sells several products together as one item at a combined price, while still tracking the stock of each item inside.

triggers: buy these together;gift set;bundle and save;package of products;meal combo;kit with several items;sell as a set
requirements: Calculate bundle stock from its parts, so it shows sold out when any part runs out;Lower the stock of every component when a bundle sells;Show what is in the bundle and the saving compared with buying separately;Split the bundle price across its parts for tax, refunds and reports;Decide how partial returns of a bundle are refunded;Let fulfillment see the individual items to pick
done_when: A bundle becomes unavailable when one part is out of stock;Selling a bundle lowers stock for each part;Refunding one part gives a predictable amount

name: Sale pricing (compare-at price)
explanation: Shows a reduced price next to the original price, such as was 50 now 35, in a way that is honest and follows price-reduction rules.

triggers: show original price crossed out;on sale price;was and now price;percentage off label;crossed out price;sale badge on products;price drop
requirements: Show a compare-at price only when it is higher than the selling price;In the EU, use the lowest price of the previous 30 days as the earlier price when announcing a reduction;Keep a history of past prices so the reference price can be checked;Start and end sales on a schedule in the shop's time zone;Do not show the old price by strikethrough alone, add text such as Was or Original price for screen readers;Round percentage-off labels so they never overstate the saving

name: Discount codes and promotions
explanation: Coupon codes and automatic deals such as 10 percent off, a fixed amount off, free shipping or buy one get one, with rules about who can use them and how often.

triggers: enter a coupon;apply promo code;percent off;buy one get one free;first order discount;free shipping coupon;discount for new customers;limit coupon to one use
requirements: Validate and apply discounts on the server at checkout, never trust a discount sent by the browser;Support limits such as minimum order, start and end dates, total uses and one use per customer;Decide which discounts can combine and apply them in a fixed order;Treat codes as case-insensitive and give a clear reason when one does not apply;Rate limit code attempts and use long random codes for one-off coupons so they cannot be guessed;Show the discount on each affected line and recompute it when the cart changes

explanation: Charges a different price per unit depending on how many are bought or used, either per tier band or one rate for the whole amount.

triggers: cheaper when you buy more;price per unit drops;bulk discount;first 100 cost this then;wholesale price for large orders;price changes with quantity
requirements: Pick graduated (each band at its own rate) or volume (all units at the rate of the tier reached) and document it;Define tier boundaries without gaps or overlaps, including whether a boundary is inclusive;Make the last tier open-ended;Show the tier table and a worked example before purchase;Allow unit prices below the smallest coin and round only the line total;Test quantities on, just below and just above every boundary

name: Gift cards
explanation: Sells prepaid cards or codes that hold a balance, which the person who receives them can spend across one or more orders.

triggers: buy a gift card;send a gift voucher by email;check gift card balance;pay with gift card;gift card code;digital gift card;redeem a voucher
requirements: Generate long random codes and show only the last few characters after issue;Rate limit balance checks and redemption attempts to stop code guessing;Treat a gift card as payment, not a discount, so tax is charged on the goods;Deduct the balance in a transaction and allow partial use across orders;Follow local laws on expiry dates and refunds of balances;Let staff disable a lost or stolen card and log every balance change

name: Store credit and prepaid credits
explanation: Keeps a credit amount on a customer account, such as a refund as store credit or prepaid usage credits, that is used up automatically by later orders or invoices.

triggers: refund as store credit;top up account balance;buy credits in advance;credits left on my account;use my balance at checkout;prepaid usage credits
requirements: Record every credit and debit as a ledger entry and compute the balance from it;Update the balance in a transaction so two orders cannot spend the same credit;Keep a separate balance per currency;Decide the order credits apply in, such as soonest to expire first;Show the balance, its history and any expiry date to the customer;Say whether credit can be refunded to the card or only spent

name: Sales tax and VAT calculation

triggers: charge vat;add tax at checkout;tax for other countries;enter vat number;tax inclusive prices;business customer without vat;tax by state
requirements: Calculate tax from the buyer's location and the product's tax category using maintained rates, not hard-coded numbers;Decide if prices include or exclude tax and show it the same way everywhere;Validate business tax IDs and apply reverse charge only when the rules allow it;Recalculate tax when the address, cart or shipping changes;Show tax as a separate line and on invoices with the details the law requires;Store the rate and amount used with each order for reporting and refunds

name: Multi-currency pricing

triggers: show prices in euros;change currency;prices in local money;currency switcher;pay in my currency;sell abroad

triggers: where is my order;track my parcel;order shipped email;out for delivery message;delivery status;tracking link

name: Wishlists and saved items

name: Donations and pay-what-you-want

name: Subscription billing

requirements: Let users choose per notification type and per channel (email, push, in-app, SMS);Keep security and legally required messages on and explain why;Offer quiet hours in the user's own time zone and hold or batch messages during them;Check preferences on the server at send time for every channel;Make unsubscribe links in emails update the same preferences;Start with sensible defaults and keep the options short and grouped;Save changes immediately and confirm them

name: Email digests
explanation: Collects many notifications into one summary email sent daily or weekly, instead of sending a separate email for each event.

name: Newsletter signup (double opt-in)
explanation: A form that collects email subscribers and sends a confirmation email, adding the person to the list only after they click to confirm, with a record of their consent.

name: Marketing email campaigns
explanation: Sends promotional or newsletter emails in bulk to a list of subscribers, following anti-spam rules such as one-click unsubscribe and sender authentication.

done_when: One-click unsubscribe works from the mail app without signing in;Unsubscribed or bounced addresses never get later campaigns;SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass for campaign emails;Every email shows the sender's postal address

name: Content management system (CMS)
explanation: Lets editors create and update the content of a website or app, such as pages, posts and their fields, without changing code.
synonyms: CMS;headless CMS;content model;content types;editorial backend
triggers: let editors change the website;edit pages without code;non-technical staff update content;manage blog posts;add new page types;content admin

triggers: save as draft;preview before publishing;publish a post;unpublish an article;share a preview link;not live yet

name: Media library
explanation: A central place where editors upload, browse, search, describe and reuse images, videos and files across all their content.

triggers: reuse uploaded images;browse uploaded files;image gallery for editors;search uploaded photos;manage images in one place;insert an image from the library
requirements: Store alt text, caption and title with each item, and allow alt text to be changed where it is used;Generate resized versions and thumbnails on upload;Let editors search and filter by type, date and name;Show where a file is used and warn before deleting one that is still in use;Validate file type and size and strip location metadata where needed;Control who can upload, edit and delete files;Keep the grid keyboard accessible and offer list and grid views

name: User-defined custom fields
